Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: room and VIC state. Hardware/banking: normal target temporarily uses $01=$34 to expose room RAM beneath ROM/I/O.

Purpose: Tail-call death handling through $CFFA. Inputs: current room/player state. Outputs: respawn or title transition. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: death handler state and hardware. Purpose: Probe the cell at working X $1014 and row $0F. Inputs: $1014,$0F. Outputs: tile code from $1024. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: X,Y,A per target. Hardware: screen/color memory read by target.

Purpose: Probe one row above working cell. Inputs: $1014,$0F. Outputs: tile code from $1024. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: X,Y,A. Hardware: screen/color memory read by target.

Purpose: Probe two rows below working cell. Inputs: $1014,$0F. Outputs: tile code from $1024. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: X,Y,A. Hardware: screen/color memory read by target.

Purpose: Run disabled selector hook, rope collision/animation work, then dispatch state $33 through $1003. Inputs: complete player/room/input state. Outputs: selected handler runs. Clobbers: A,X and shared state. Assumptions: state 0-6 and table/vector initialization. Hardware: rope work stages sprite data for the IRQ.

Purpose: Shared tail-call landing that stages this tick's three rope sprites and then falls into the state-table dispatch at $107E. Inputs: no register is read here; the single JSR reads room_has_rope $0402, rope_animation_divider $1018, rope_oscillator_position $0403 and the pointer table at $1856. Both external callers arrive with A holding the byte just read from $D01E and with N and Z set from it ($1B08 in update_player_attached_to_rope, $1BAD in handle_rope_tile_collision), and with player_state $33 already forced to 2 and $51/$53 cleared; that A is dead because $107E immediately reloads $33. On the internal fallthrough from $1078 the registers are whatever attach_player_to_rope_if_colliding left. Outputs: on every second rope tick, staged sprite bytes $0500-$05BF, staged coordinates $05C0-$05C5, handshake $0407 = $FF and an advanced oscillator; then control falls through to $107E. Nothing returns to the caller. Assumptions: both external entries are JMP tail calls, so this block owns no return address. From $1B0B the surrounding state-6 handler was itself entered by JMP ($1011) at $108E and owns no frame either, so the topmost stack word still belongs to the game main loop; from $1BB0 the JSR return address pushed at $1B49, $1B4D, $1B52, $1B56, $1B5B or $1B5F is abandoned and never popped. Nothing unwinds it here: the stack pointer is reclaimed wholesale by the LDX #$FF / TXS at $3349 or $334F that terminates the tick. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, zero page $07, $08 and $31, and the rope staging state, all through produce_rope_sprite_staging. Hardware: the callers' reads of $D01E have already cleared the VIC-II sprite/sprite collision latch; produce_rope_sprite_staging sets sprite-enable bits 5-7 in $D015 and clears X-MSB bits 5-7 in $D010. The staged bytes only become visible to VIC-II when the raster IRQ copies them to $6B00-$6BBF at $353F.

Purpose: Select the handler for the current player state from the seven-entry table at $1003-$1010 and enter it through the mutable indirect target $1011. Inputs: player_state $33, which must be 0-6, and the table itself. No register input: A is reloaded from $33 at once, so the caller's A, X and flags are dead. The one external caller, $1B34 in update_player_attached_to_rope, arrives with A holding the byte just read from $D01E at $1B31 and with $33 already set to 1, jump direction $1013 copied from manual direction $49, and $52, $51 and $53 cleared - it is a jump-off-the-rope transition, not a state query. Outputs: writes the selected handler address into $1011/$1012 and jumps through it; control never returns here. Assumptions: the external entry is a JMP tail call, so this block owns no return address; state 6 was itself entered by JMP ($1011) and owns no frame, so the topmost stack word is still the game main loop's, and nothing between here and the LDX #$FF / TXS at $3349 or $334F unwinds it. The ASL/TAX index is unchecked, so a $33 above 6 would read past the table. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the writable pointer $1011/$1012. Y is preserved into the handler. Hardware: none at this address; the entered handler may drive VIC-II, SID or CIA state.

Purpose: Player state 0 grounded movement, jumps, edge exits, and tile interactions. Inputs: manual direction $49, jump $4A, player coordinates/state. Outputs: movement or state/room transition. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A,X,Y and player temporaries. Hardware: tile probes read screen/color state.

Purpose: Two-instruction fork that sends grounded horizontal movement to the right-moving path at $10CC or the left-moving path at $112A according to the sign of the signed direction byte the caller has just loaded. Inputs: the N flag only. Internally $10C2 reaches here with N from LDA $49 at $10C0 and only when manual direction $49 is non-zero; externally $1535 in update_player_on_conveyor reaches here with N from LDA $13 at $1533, the room's signed conveyor direction, with no preceding zero test, so a $13 of $00 takes the BPL branch to $10CC. A itself is never re-read: both destinations reload from $32 and $4F. Outputs: control transfers to $10CC or $112A; no memory and no register is written. Assumptions: the external entry is a JMP tail call inside player state 4, and that handler was entered by JMP ($1011) at $108E, so no return address of state 4 or of this block is on the stack and the topmost stack word belongs to the game main loop. This block never reads $33, so it cannot and must not distinguish state 0 from state 4; the state-dependent part of grounded movement lives further on in handle_ground_support_tile $11C4, which does read $33. Clobbers: nothing - only PC changes. A, X, Y and all flags pass through unchanged. Hardware: none.

Purpose: Move the player one step to the right in grounded movement - advance the sub-cell phase and facing frame, cross into the next cell when the phase wraps, take the right-hand room exit at column $1F, and probe the tiles being entered. Inputs: player_horizontal_phase $32, player_x_cell $4F, facing frame $50, working tile row $0F, tile probe X $1014, and previous_exit_right $20 on the exit path. No register input: LDA $32 overwrites A on the first instruction. Internally $10C7 arrives with N clear; externally $15ED in enter_or_reconcile_conveyor arrives with A holding resolved_conveyor_direction $1017, known non-negative because $15E8 took BPL. Both values are dead. Outputs: updated $32 and $50, $4F incremented on a cell crossing, tile probes with grounded and ground-support handling; or, at column $1F with phase below 2, $0E loaded from $20, $33 = 2, $51 = 0, $53 = 0 followed by prepare_room_via_vector $1027. Every path leaves through $1021, $1027 or the shared continuation at $11B1; nothing returns. Assumptions: the external entry is a JMP tail call inside player state 5, which was entered by JMP ($1011) and owns no return address, so the topmost stack word is the game main loop's and this block must not attempt to RTS. Reaching this address does not imply state 0: states 4 and 5 both route their resolved direction here, and the block itself never reads $33. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags; $32, $50, $0F, $1014 and, on a cell crossing, $4F; $07-$0A through initialize_tile_location and lookup_tile_at_cell; plus anything the tile handlers change, including $33, $51, $53, item state and an unconditional transfer to kill_player $15F0 on fire contact. Hardware: the tile probes read extended-colour screen codes from screen RAM at $7C00-$7FFF in VIC bank 1 through lookup_tile_via_vector; the room-exit path hands all VIC-II reconfiguration to prepare_room_entry $2DC6.

Purpose: Move the player one step to the left in grounded movement - advance the sub-cell phase and facing frame downwards, cross into the previous cell when the phase underflows, take the left-hand room exit at cell 0 phase 0, and probe the tiles being entered. Inputs: player_x_cell $4F, player_horizontal_phase $32, facing frame $50, working tile row $0F, tile probe X $1014, and previous_exit_left $1F on the exit path. No register input: LDA $4F / ORA $32 overwrites A on the first two instructions. Internally $10C9 arrives with N set; externally $15EA in enter_or_reconcile_conveyor arrives with A holding resolved_conveyor_direction $1017, known negative because $15E8 did not take BPL. Both values are dead. Outputs: updated $32 and $50 with facing bit 2 forced by ORA #$04, $4F decremented on a cell crossing, tile probes with grounded and ground-support handling; or, when $4F and $32 are both zero, $0E loaded from $1F, $33 = 2, $51 = 0, $53 = 0 followed by prepare_room_via_vector $1027. Every path leaves through $1021, $1027 or the shared continuation at $11B1; nothing returns. Assumptions: the external entry is a JMP tail call inside player state 5, which was entered by JMP ($1011) and owns no return address, so the topmost stack word is the game main loop's and this block must not attempt to RTS. Reaching this address does not imply state 0: state 5 routes a negative resolved direction here, and the block itself never reads $33. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags; $32, $50, $0F, $1014 and, on a cell crossing, $4F; $07-$0A through initialize_tile_location and lookup_tile_at_cell; plus anything the tile handlers change, including $33, $51, $53, item state and an unconditional transfer to kill_player $15F0 on fire contact. Hardware: the tile probes read extended-colour screen codes from screen RAM at $7C00-$7FFF in VIC bank 1 through lookup_tile_via_vector; the room-exit path hands all VIC-II reconfiguration to prepare_room_entry $2DC6.

Purpose: Dispatch grounded contact tile codes for solid, ramp, fire, item, and ordinary continuation. Inputs: A tile code, direction/ramp state. Outputs: state transition, death, item collection, or return. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A and called helpers. Hardware: none directly.

Purpose: Process the supporting tile beneath grounded Willy after an 18-byte NOP lead. Inputs: A=tile code plus valid player and conveyor state. Outputs: enters conveyor motion, triggers fire death, collects an item, or returns without a state change. Assumptions: current-room collision buffers and player state are valid. Clobbers: A and player state. Hardware: none directly.

Purpose: Player state 2 falling, fall-duration accounting, landing, and downward room exit. Inputs: player coordinates and fall counters. Outputs: moved player, new room/state, or lethal-fall death. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A,X,Y and player state. Hardware: tile probes read screen/color state.

Purpose: Player state 1 jump curve and horizontal/vertical collision handling. Inputs: jump index $52, direction, coordinates, delta table. Outputs: moved player, landing/fall/room transition, item or death. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A,X,Y and player state. Hardware: tile probes read screen/color state.

Purpose: Probe upper cells during ascent. Inputs: current jump position and direction. Outputs: A/carry and collision path selection. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A,X,Y and tile temporaries. Hardware: screen/color state read through tile lookup.

Purpose: Resolve ceiling contact with solid, fire, and item tiles. Inputs: tile code from ascent probes. Outputs: continued jump, item collection, or death. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A and called helpers. Hardware: none directly.

Purpose: Probe cells below Willy during descending jump motion. Inputs: player position/direction. Outputs: landing tile classification. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A,X,Y and tile temporaries. Hardware: screen/color state read through tile lookup.

Purpose: Resolve landing on solid, fire, item, ramp, or conveyor tiles. Inputs: tile code and movement state. Outputs: grounded/ramp/conveyor state, item collection, or death. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A and player state. Hardware: none directly.

Purpose: Advance right-moving jump, including screen-edge room transitions and side collisions. Inputs: player coordinates/jump state. Outputs: updated position or transition. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A,X,Y and player state. Hardware: tile probes read display state.

Purpose: Apply the current step of the 36-entry jump curve to the player's vertical pixel position and advance a right-moving jump by one horizontal sub-cell, crossing into the next cell when the phase wraps. Inputs: jump_curve_index $52, the signed vertical delta table at $102D, player_y $1C, player_horizontal_phase $32 and player_x_cell $4F. No register input: X is reloaded from $52 and A from the table. The external caller $0FDB in jump_right_collision_trampoline arrives with A = 1, the player state it has just compared, and Z set by the CMP #$01 at $0FD4; that value is dead here. C is cleared locally by the CLC at $1372, so the caller's carry does not matter. Outputs: updated $1C; then either the cell-aligned branch at $13AC, which takes the right-hand room exit at column $1F or runs the right-tile collision probes, or a phase advance that continues into the curve step at $138F. Nothing returns. Assumptions: $0FDB is a JMP tail call, and $0FD2 was itself reached by JMP from $1401 inside advance_jump_right, so neither owns a return address; player state 1 was entered by JMP ($1011), so the topmost stack word still belongs to the game main loop. $52 must be below $24 - the indexed table read is unchecked - and the caller guarantees this only by having come through the curve. Clobbers: A, X, flags, $1C and, on a cell crossing, $4F, $32 and $50; Y is preserved by this block but not by the probe paths it falls into, which also clobber $0F, $1014 and $07-$0A. Hardware: none at this address; the collision probes it reaches read screen RAM at $7C00-$7FFF in VIC bank 1, and the room-exit path hands VIC-II reconfiguration to prepare_room_entry $2DC6.

Purpose: Advance the jump curve index by one and, when the 36-step curve is exhausted at index $24, end the jump by clearing the curve and fall counters and switching the player to falling state 2; then leave through the main-loop continuation vector. Inputs: jump_curve_index $52. No register input: A is reloaded from $52 by the LDA at $1391. The external caller $14BC in handle_horizontal_jump_collision arrives with A = 2, the contacted tile code it has just compared, and Z set by the CMP #$02 at $14B8; that value is dead. Outputs: $52 incremented, or $52 = $51 = 0 and $33 = 2 at curve end; control leaves through continue_main_loop_via_vector $1021 in every case. Assumptions: this is the right-moving jump's curve step, but handle_horizontal_jump_collision is JSR-called from advance_jump_right at $13C5, $13CD and $13DB and from advance_jump_left at $1469, $1471 and $147F, so a left-moving jump that contacts tile code 2 also lands here and skips the left routine's own equivalent step at $1444. In every case $14BC abandons the JSR return address that handle_horizontal_jump_collision was entered with: it is never popped, and the stack is reclaimed only by the LDX #$FF / TXS at $334F reached through $1021. Clobbers: A and flags; $52, and at curve end $51 and $33. X and Y are preserved. Hardware: none directly; the vector target $334F resets the stack pointer and drives SID voice 3 when the collected-item count has changed.

Purpose: Advance left-moving jump, including screen-edge room transitions and side collisions. Inputs: player coordinates/jump state. Outputs: updated position or transition. Assumptions: the active phase is initialized and the stated inputs and state are valid. Clobbers: A,X,Y and player state. Hardware: tile probes read display state.

Purpose: Apply the current step of the 36-entry jump curve to the player's vertical pixel position and advance a left-moving jump by one horizontal sub-cell, crossing into the previous cell when the phase underflows. Inputs: jump_curve_index $52, the signed vertical delta table at $102D, player_y $1C, player_x_cell $4F, player_horizontal_phase $32 and previous_exit_left $1F on the exit path. No register input: X is reloaded from $52 and A from the table. The external caller $0FEF in jump_left_collision_trampoline arrives with A = 1, the player state it has just compared, and Z set by the CMP #$01 at $0FE8; that value is dead. C is cleared locally by the CLC at $1414, so the caller's carry does not matter. Outputs: updated $1C; then either the left-edge room exit when $4F and $32 are both zero - $0E loaded from $1F, $1C forced even, prepare_room_via_vector $1027 - or a phase decrement, or the left-tile collision probes at $1463. Nothing returns. Assumptions: $0FEF is a JMP tail call, and $0FE6 was itself reached by JMP from $14A6 inside advance_jump_left, so neither owns a return address; player state 1 was entered by JMP ($1011), so the topmost stack word still belongs to the game main loop. $52 must be below $24 - the indexed table read is unchecked. Clobbers: A, X, flags, $1C and, on a cell crossing, $4F, $32 and $50; Y is preserved by this block but not by the probe paths it falls into, which also clobber $0F, $1014 and $07-$0A. Hardware: none at this address; the collision probes it reaches read screen RAM at $7C00-$7FFF in VIC bank 1, and the room-exit path hands VIC-II reconfiguration to prepare_room_entry $2DC6.

Purpose: Discard the entire hardware stack with LDX #$FF / TXS and enter the player update at player_tick_entry $1000. It serves both as the tail of schedule_player_update's sixth-pass path and as the standing target of the player redispatch vector. Inputs: none in registers. X is overwritten immediately; A, Y and the flags carried in are never read. Externally it is entered through JMP ($CFF2) at redispatch_player_via_vector $101E, whose callers have just written a new player state to $33 and expect $1000 to dispatch it: $10BD and $15AB and $15E2 and $1530 set state 1, $119F sets state 3, $1580 and $1599 set state 4. $CFF2/$CFF3 hold $49/$33, that is $3349, stored by LDA #$49 / STA $CFF2 at $2D48-$2D4A and LDA #$33 / STA $CFF3 at $2D4D-$2D4F during initialize_game. Outputs: SP = $FF and control passes to $1000. It never returns and cannot: the return address of whatever called it has just been discarded. Assumptions: unusually for a routine entry, this block deliberately destroys its caller's stack frame and every frame beneath it. That is precisely the engine's mechanism for tolerating tail-jumps out of JSR-called helpers - $119F leaves handle_grounded_tile, entered by JSR from $110F, $1117, $116F and $1177, without ever executing its RTS, and $14BC leaves handle_horizontal_jump_collision the same way. Consequently nothing may be held on the stack across this address, it must never be reached by JSR expecting a return, and callers must have committed all state to memory before jumping. Only the stack pointer is reset; the bytes in page 1 are left as they are. Clobbers: X, set to $FF; SP, set to $FF; N and Z from the LDX. A, Y, C, V and all memory are untouched. Hardware: none. Interrupts are not masked here, so a raster IRQ taken immediately after the TXS pushes onto the freshly reset stack at $01FF downwards, which is the intended behaviour.
